8 13-03-2023 CWJC No.1407 of 2022 Learned counsel for the petitioner admits that the tower has already been erected on the land and part of the compensation has been paid to him, however, he claims additional amount.

2. Keeping in view the provisions of the Indian Telegraphic Act, 1885 and the Electricity Act, 2003,
the petitioner has statutory remedy to make a reference before the concerned District Judge, who can examine the claim and pass suitable orders accordingly.
3. Granting liberty to the petitioner as aforesaid, the writ petition stands dismissed as not maintenable.
4. Interlocutory Application, if any, shall stand disposed of.
CWJC No.8401 of 2019 5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has not been paid a single penny as compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the Company states that as on date, no work has commenced on the land of the petitioner.

He submits that if any pole is constructed on the said land and the extension line is drawn over and above the property of the petitioner, suitable compensation shall be Patna High Court CWJC No.1407 of 2022(8) dt.13-03-2023 awarded.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the compensation should be awarded to him as per the existing norms.

8. This Court is of the firm opinion that the issue with regard to the amount of the compensation to be paid is to be adjudicated exclusively by the concerned District Judge upon a reference being made, if the concerned party is dissatisfied with the compensation already offered to him.
Upon such reference being made, the District Judge shall examine and pass suitable orders.
The writ petition in this regard is not maintainable.
This Court is also of the view that the writ petition is premature.
9. In view of the above, the writ petition is dismissed with aforesaid liberty.

Learned counsel for the petitioners prays to withdraw the writ petitions with liberty to take up the matter before the concerned District Judge and make a reference for Patna High Court CWJC No.1407 of 2022(8) dt.13-03-2023 claiming compensation with respect to the erection of electricity poles for high tension line in terms of the India Telegraphic Act, 1885 and the Electricity Act, 2003.
He also submits that in terms of the circular issued by the Central Government of 2015, the compensation should be awarded to him accordingly.

12. While granting liberty to the petitioners to withdraw these petitions, it is observed that the learned concerned District Judge shall examine the aspects and also consider whether the compensation is to be paid in terms of the Circular of 2015 or as per the original provisions.
13. The respective parties shall be free to take up all the pleadings before the concerned District Judge.
14. The District Judge would also be empowered to examine whether the interest is required to be paid on the amount.
15. The writ petitions are dismissed as withdrawn with aforesaid liberty.

(Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, J) Chn/-
